description: A Go export whose doc comment (or whose group's doc comment) carries @hexa:public is marked hexa_public and is never reported dead; untagged Go, TypeScript and Rust exports behave as before.

specs.description: A tagged exported Go function is public
specs.given: A Go file whose line `// Build makes a client. @hexa:public` sits directly above `func Build() *Client {}`
specs.then: The export named `Build`, of kind Function, has hexa_public == true

specs.description: The tag may be on any line of a multi-line doc comment
specs.given: A Go file with three consecutive `//` lines directly above `func New() {}`, the second of which is `// @hexa:public` and the others plain prose
specs.then: The export `New` has hexa_public == true

specs.description: A tagged method is public
specs.given: A Go file with `type Client struct{}` and, directly above `func (c *Client) Send() error { return nil }`, the line `// @hexa:public`
specs.then: The export `Send`, of kind Method, has hexa_public == true

specs.description: Tagged standalone type, const and var declarations are public
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public` directly above each of `type Option struct{}`, `const MaxRetries = 3` and `var DefaultTimeout = 5`
specs.then: The exports `Option`, `MaxRetries` and `DefaultTimeout` each have hexa_public == true

specs.description: A tagged Go export with no caller is not reported dead
specs.given: A project in which one Go file declares `// @hexa:public` above `func Build() {}` and no other file names `Build`
specs.when: The project is analysed for dead exports
specs.then: No DeadExport with export_name `Build` is reported

specs.description: A comment separated from the declaration by a blank line is not its doc comment
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public`, then one blank line, then `func Build() {}`
specs.then: The export `Build` has hexa_public == false

specs.description: The run ends at a line that is not a comment
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public` directly above `func Helper() {}`, followed directly by `func Build() {}` with no comment of its own
specs.then: `Helper` has hexa_public == true and `Build` has hexa_public == false

specs.description: A tag in the body of another declaration or inside a function does not mark the next export
specs.given: A Go file whose `func A() {` body ends with the line `// @hexa:public` before its closing `}`, followed directly by `func B() {}`
specs.then: Neither `A` nor `B` has hexa_public == true

specs.description: A doc comment without the tag does not make an export public
specs.given: A Go file with `// Build makes a client.` directly above `func Build() {}`
specs.then: The export `Build` has hexa_public == false

specs.description: A tagged export with no caller elsewhere is still not reported dead even though unused
specs.given: A project with one Go file declaring `// @hexa:public` above `const Unused = 1`, named nowhere else
specs.when: The project is analysed for dead exports
specs.then: `Unused` is absent from dead_exports, and the dead-export count does not include it

specs.description: For every exported Go declaration, hexa_public is exactly whether the contiguous comment run above it contains the tag
specs.given: Any Go file built from functions, methods, type, const and var declarations with upper-case names, each preceded by an arbitrary run of `//` lines, optionally containing `@hexa:public` on any line, optionally separated from the declaration by blank lines
specs.then: For each export, hexa_public is true if and only if some line in the uninterrupted run of `//` lines ending on the line directly above its declaration contains `@hexa:public`

specs.description: A tag on a const group marks every spec in it
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public` directly above `const (`, which holds `A = 1`, `B = 2` and `C = 3` with no comments of their own
specs.then: `A`, `B` and `C` each have hexa_public == true

specs.description: A tag on one spec inside a group marks only that spec
specs.given: A Go file with an untagged `type (` group holding `Alpha struct{}`, then `// @hexa:public` directly above `Beta struct{}`, then `Gamma struct{}`
specs.then: `Beta` has hexa_public == true; `Alpha` and `Gamma` have hexa_public == false

specs.description: A tag on a var group covers its specs
specs.given: A Go file with a two-line doc comment, the second line `// @hexa:public`, directly above `var (`, which holds `X = 1` and `Y = 2`
specs.then: `X` and `Y` each have hexa_public == true

specs.description: A group comment separated from the group by a blank line does not cover it
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public`, then a blank line, then `const (` holding `A = 1` and `B = 2`
specs.then: `A` and `B` have hexa_public == false

specs.description: A spec's own tag does not spread to its siblings
specs.given: A Go file with an untagged `const (` group in which `// @hexa:public` sits directly above `A = 1`, followed by `B = 2`
specs.then: `A` has hexa_public == true and `B` has hexa_public == false

specs.description: A group's tag does not cover a declaration after the group
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public` above `const (` holding `A = 1`, closed by `)`, followed directly by `const B = 2`
specs.then: `A` has hexa_public == true and `B` has hexa_public == false

specs.description: A grouped spec is public exactly when its own run or the group's run carries the tag
specs.given: Any Go file with type, const and var groups of exported specs, where the group and each spec are preceded by arbitrary comment runs, each run optionally containing `@hexa:public` and optionally separated by blank lines
specs.then: For each grouped spec, hexa_public is true if and only if the tag is in the contiguous comment run directly above the spec or in the contiguous comment run directly above its group's keyword

specs.description: An untagged Go project grades as before
specs.given: A Go project with no `@hexa:public` anywhere, one exported function `Orphan` named by no other file
specs.then: `Orphan` is reported in dead_exports, every Go export has hexa_public == false, and health_score equals compute_health_score over the same counts as before the change

specs.description: TypeScript and Rust still read the tag as before
specs.given: A TypeScript file with `/** @hexa:public */` above `export function build() {}` and a Rust file with `/// @hexa:public` above `pub fn build() {}`
specs.when: extract_exports is called with the matching language
specs.then: Each `build` export has hexa_public == true

specs.description: Untagged TypeScript and Rust exports do not become public
specs.given: A TypeScript file with `export function f() {}` and a Rust file with `pub fn f() {}`, neither with any comment
specs.when: extract_exports is called with the matching language
specs.then: Each `f` export has hexa_public == false

specs.description: The tag does not change any other field of a Go export
specs.given: A Go file with `// @hexa:public` directly above `func Build() {}` on line 2
specs.then: The `Build` export has name `Build`, line 2, kind Function, and only hexa_public differs from the untagged version of the same file

specs.description: For any input with no tag, exports and grade are unchanged
specs.given: Any Go, TypeScript or Rust source in which no comment contains `@hexa:public`
specs.when: extract_exports is called and the project is analysed
specs.then: Every export has hexa_public == false, and the exports, dead_exports and health_score are identical to those produced before the change
